# SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS support in mojo's own crypto + stop filevault reading SECRET_KEY from the DB

- **Kind**: feature (security hardening)
- **Date**: 2026-07-30
- **Requested by**: Ian

Apply rules: `django-mojo-build-conventions`, `nativemojo-board-conventions`.

> **Scope was reduced on 2026-07-30, mid-scoping.** This item originally asked
> django-mojo to hard-fail at startup on a placeholder `SECRET_KEY`. Ian
> investigated and established the premise was wrong: `SETYOUROWNKEY` lives only
> in **private** repos, not in the public django-mojo framework, so it is a
> shared-known key rather than a published one. The hard fail is dropped —
> see "Dropped scope" below for what was cut and why, so this is not
> re-proposed later.

## Description

Make a `SECRET_KEY` rotation survivable in django-mojo. Django ships
`SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` so old signatures still verify after a key change, but it
only covers Django's own signing. Every django-mojo consumer reads raw
`settings.SECRET_KEY` and knows nothing about fallbacks, so rotating the key
today silently breaks mojo-issued tokens and makes filevault files
undecryptable.

Teach mojo's own verify/unwrap paths to honor `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, so the
downstream repos can strip their placeholder keys and set a real one without
destroying data.

Second, unrelated defect found while scoping: filevault reads `SECRET_KEY`
through the DB-overridable settings path, making the file key-wrapping secret
settable at runtime.

## Context

### What SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS actually covers

Verified against the Django 5.2.16 in this repo's `.venv` — exactly three
consumers, all **verification-only** (a fallback is never used to sign new
values):

- `django/core/signing.py:137,209` — signed cookies, `Signer`, `TimestampSigner`
- `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:32` — password-reset tokens
- `django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:142` — session auth hash

So adding `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS = ["SETYOUROWNKEY"]` in a consumer repo keeps
sessions and password-reset links working across a key change — and does nothing
for anything mojo signs or wraps.

### The mojo-side surfaces that need it

| Surface | File | Key use |
|---|---|---|
| Bouncer auth tokens | `mojo/apps/account/services/bouncer/token_manager.py:19-25`, verify at `:88` | HMAC signing key derived from `SECRET_KEY` + label |
| Bouncer assess signature | `mojo/apps/account/rest/bouncer/assess.py:257` (issue), `:329` (verify) | `crypto_sign(data)` with the default key = `settings.SECRET_KEY`, verified by recompute-and-compare |
| filevault ekey unwrap | `mojo/apps/filevault/services/vault.py:124,169,324` | `unwrap_ekey(..., SECRET_KEY, uuid)` — passphrase is `SECRET_KEY + file_uuid` (`mojo/helpers/crypto/vault.py:140-160`) |
| filevault access token | `mojo/apps/filevault/services/vault.py:232` → `crypto_vault.validate_access_token` (`mojo/helpers/crypto/vault.py:246`) | `SECRET_KEY` |

**Not affected — deliberately:**

- **Webhook HMAC** (`mojo/helpers/crypto/sign.py`). Its `secret_key=None`
  default resolves to `settings.SECRET_KEY`, but every real caller passes an
  explicit per-group secret: `mojo/helpers/request.py:178`
  (`group.get_webhook_secret()`), `mojo/apps/incident/rest/maestro_webhook.py:42`
  (link key), `mojo/apps/account/utils/tokens.py:82,119`
  (`user.get_auth_key()`). Those secrets are per-Group/per-User DB values, not
  `SECRET_KEY`, so a `SECRET_KEY` rotation does not touch them. No change.
- **`mojo/helpers/crypto/hash.py:17`** (salt defaults to `SECRET_KEY`). Its
  output is used as a **stored lookup key** (e.g. an `ssn_hash` column queried
  by equality), not as a signature verified against a known input. Fallbacks
  cannot help a lookup: you cannot query N ways and call it a match. Rotating
  the key requires re-hashing the stored column — a data migration in the
  consumer repo, out of scope here. **This limitation must be documented
  explicitly**, because it is the one case where the fallback mechanism looks
  like it should help and does not.

### The filevault DB-override defect

`mojo/apps/filevault/services/vault.py:18` reads
`settings.get("SECRET_KEY", "")`. `SettingsHelper.get()` consults the
DB/Redis-backed `Setting` table first (`mojo/helpers/settings/helper.py:166-178`);
`get_static()` reads file-based settings only (`helper.py:180-198`). Every other
`SECRET_KEY` consumer uses the attribute path, which routes to `get_static`.

So a `Setting` row named `SECRET_KEY` — creatable over REST by any holder of
`manage_settings`/`groups` (`mojo/apps/account/models/setting.py:24,36-39`) —
would silently re-key filevault's per-file wrapping while leaving everything
else on the file-based key. `docs/django_developer/helpers/settings.md:150`
already documents the rule this violates ("`get_static()` for conf-file-only
keys"). Same class as item #50.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new shared accessor yields the primary `SECRET_KEY` followed by each entry of `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, read file-based only (`get_static`)
- [ ] Bouncer token verification (`token_manager.py:88`) accepts a token signed under a fallback key; token *issuance* always uses the primary key
- [ ] Bouncer assess signature verification (`assess.py:329`) accepts a signature produced under a fallback key; issuance uses the primary
- [ ] filevault `unwrap_ekey` and `validate_access_token` try the primary key then each fallback; `wrap_ekey` and token creation always use the primary
- [ ] `mojo/apps/filevault/services/vault.py:18` uses `get_static`, so a DB `Setting` row named `SECRET_KEY` cannot re-key filevault
- [ ] Absent/empty `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` changes no existing behavior — every current test still passes unmodified
- [ ] Fallbacks are **never** used to sign, wrap, or issue — verify/unwrap only
- [ ] `hash.py`'s inability to use fallbacks is documented, with the re-key migration noted as the consumer's responsibility
- [ ] `bin/run_tests --agent` green against the baseline captured before the first edit
- [ ] Docs: `docs/django_developer/helpers/settings_reference.md`, `helpers/settings.md`, `helpers/crypto.md`, `filevault/README.md`
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` — new capability + the rotation procedure

## Investigation

- **What exists**: the four surfaces in the table above; `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`
  is referenced nowhere in this repo today (no grep hits outside `.venv`).
- **What changes**: verify/unwrap paths gain a fallback loop; one settings read
  is corrected.
- **Constraints**:
  - Django's global default for `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` is `[]`
    (`django/conf/global_settings.py:276`), so `get_static(..., [])` is always
    safe and the no-fallback path is the existing behavior byte for byte.
  - The accessor must use `get_static`, not `get` — a DB-settable fallback list
    would be a runtime-injectable key-acceptance list, i.e. an auth bypass.
  - Fallback iteration must not leak timing: keep using `hmac.compare_digest`
    per candidate, as the current code does.
- **Related files**: `mojo/helpers/crypto/vault.py`, `mojo/helpers/crypto/sign.py`
  (read-only, no change), `mojo/apps/account/services/bouncer/token_manager.py`,
  `mojo/apps/account/rest/bouncer/assess.py`,
  `mojo/apps/filevault/services/vault.py`, `mojo/helpers/settings/helper.py`

## Dropped scope — do not re-propose without new evidence

The original ask was a startup hard-fail on placeholder `SECRET_KEY` values.
Cut on 2026-07-30 because the premise did not hold: the placeholders live in
private repos, so this is a shared-known key, not a leaked one. Also cut with
it: the placeholder constant list, the minimum-length floor, and the
no-escape-hatch rule.

Two findings from that investigation are worth keeping on the record, because
they are the reason a placeholder ever ends up live:

1. **The only key generator throws its key away.** `check_var()` in the starter
   repos' `bin/paths.py:77-85` generates a 50-char key, writes it, then calls
   `Path.write_text()` four more times on the same file — each truncating. Only
   the last line survives. Tracked in #969 / #970.
2. **The deploy path never writes a `SECRET_KEY`.** `aws/deploy.py:write_django_conf()`
   emits a managed block and, per its own docstring, preserves "anything else in
   the file (SECRET_KEY, ...)" — it preserves a value it never creates.

Direct evidence: `maestro/api/var/django.conf` holds exactly `AWS_KEY`,
`AWS_REGION`, `AWS_SECRET`, `OPENAPI_DOCS_KEY` — no `SECRET_KEY`, and
`OPENAPI_DOCS_KEY` surviving alone is the exact fingerprint of the truncation
bug. (Local dev checkout; `var/` is gitignored and no production host was
inspected.)

Companion items **#969** (django-mojo-skeleton) and **#970**
(django-mojo-example) remove the placeholders from **every** profile — not just
`defaults/` — because `local/` (`PUT IN YOUR var/django.conf`) and `test/`
(`HOAISABAAJALKLJIWCC`) are non-empty and would keep Django's native empty-key
error from ever firing. The other seven consumer repos are the repo owners' call
and are not tracked here.

## Out of scope

- Any startup validation of `SECRET_KEY` (dropped, above).
- Re-keying or migrating already-persisted derived data (filevault ekeys,
  camaccess master keys, mverify `ssn_hash`). Fallbacks let *verification*
  survive a rotation; re-encrypting stored material is each consumer repo's job.
- The seven non-starter consumer repos.
- `mojo/helpers/crypto/sign.py` — callers pass explicit per-group secrets.

## Plan

### Objective

`SECRET_KEY` can be rotated without invalidating mojo-issued bouncer tokens or
bricking filevault files, by listing the old key in `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`.
Fallbacks verify and unwrap only — never sign, wrap, or issue. Separately,
filevault stops resolving `SECRET_KEY` through the DB-backed settings store.

### Implementation steps

**1. Shared accessor — `mojo/helpers/crypto/keys.py` (new)**

```python
def secret_keys():
    """Primary SECRET_KEY first, then each SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS entry.

    File-based only (get_static): a DB-settable fallback list would be a
    runtime-injectable key-acceptance list. Verify/unwrap paths iterate this;
    sign/wrap paths use secret_keys()[0].
    """
```

Reads `settings.get_static("SECRET_KEY", "")` and
`settings.get_static("SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS", [])`, drops empties, de-dupes while
preserving order, returns a list. With no fallbacks configured it returns
`[SECRET_KEY]` — so every call site's behavior is unchanged by construction.

**2. Bouncer tokens — `token_manager.py`**

Refactor `_get_signing_key()` (line 19) to `_signing_keys()` returning one
derived key per entry of `secret_keys()`, preserving the existing
`HMAC(secret, label)` derivation. Line 72 (issue) uses `[0]`. Line 88 (verify)
loops candidates, keeping `hmac.compare_digest` per candidate and returning on
first match.

**3. Bouncer assess — `assess.py:329`**

`crypto_sign(data)` currently defaults to `settings.SECRET_KEY`. Issuance
(line 257) stays on the primary. Verification recomputes `expected_sig` per
candidate key and compares each with `compare_digest`. Note the existing `[:16]`
truncation is preserved as-is — changing it is out of scope.

**4. filevault — `mojo/apps/filevault/services/vault.py`**

- Line 18: `settings.get(...)` → `settings.get_static(...)`, and rename to make
  the primary/candidates split explicit.
- Lines 67, 281 (`wrap_ekey`) and the access-token creation at ~219: primary key
  only.
- Lines 124, 169, 324 (`unwrap_ekey`) and 232 (`validate_access_token`): try
  each candidate, return the first success. `unwrap_ekey` raises `ValueError` on
  GCM auth failure (`mojo/helpers/crypto/vault.py:157-172`), so the loop catches
  `ValueError` per candidate and re-raises the original error if all fail — the
  final exception must not become "fallback 2 failed", which would be a
  confusing regression in the error message.

Keep the loop in the filevault service layer, not in `mojo/helpers/crypto/vault.py`.
The crypto helpers stay single-key primitives; policy about which keys are
acceptable belongs one layer up. This also keeps `crypto/vault.py` unit tests
untouched.

### Design decisions

1. **Verify-only, mirroring Django.** A fallback never signs or wraps. Otherwise
   a rotation never actually completes — new material keeps getting produced
   under the old key.
2. **`get_static`, never `get`.** A DB-settable `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` would let
   anyone with settings-write permission add a key the system then accepts
   signatures from. That is a direct auth bypass, and it is the same defect this
   item fixes in filevault.
3. **The fallback loop lives at the service layer, not in the crypto helpers.**
   Primitives stay single-key and independently testable.
4. **`hash.py` is left alone and documented instead.** Its output is a stored
   lookup key; multi-key lookup is not a thing. Pretending fallbacks help here
   would be worse than saying plainly that a rotation needs a re-hash migration.
5. **No new settings.** `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` is Django's own key, already
   defaulted to `[]`, already validated by `security.W025`.

### Edge cases

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` unset | `secret_keys()` → `[SECRET_KEY]`; identical to today |
| Set to `[]` | same |
| Contains the primary key too | de-duped; verified once |
| Contains an empty string | dropped by the accessor (an empty candidate would make `unwrap` attempts meaningless and could mask a real failure) |
| Parsed from `var/django.conf` as a bare string, not a list | `_parse_list_value` handles `[...]` syntax (`parser.py:97-105`); a non-list value is coerced to a single-element list by the accessor rather than iterated character by character — **this is the sharpest footgun in the change and needs a dedicated test** |
| All candidates fail to unwrap an ekey | re-raise the **primary** key's `ValueError`, not the last fallback's |
| Fallback list is long | verification cost is linear; acceptable — the list is operator-set and transitional |

### Testing plan

New `tests/test_helpers/test_secret_key_fallbacks.py` plus additions to the
existing filevault and bouncer suites. testit, `@th.django_unit_test()`, module
imported inside each test, every assert carrying a failure message.

- `secret_keys()`: unset → `[SECRET_KEY]`; with fallbacks → correct order;
  de-dupe; empty entries dropped; **a string-instead-of-list value yields one
  element, not one per character**
- Bouncer: mint a token under key A, move A to fallbacks, set key B, assert the
  token still verifies; assert a token minted *after* the rotation verifies
  under B and **not** under A alone (proves issuance uses the primary)
- filevault: wrap an ekey under key A, rotate to B with A in fallbacks, assert
  download/decrypt succeeds; assert newly uploaded files wrap under B
- filevault DB-override: create a `Setting` row named `SECRET_KEY`, assert
  `_get_secret_key()` ignores it. Per `.claude/rules/testing.md`, delete the row
  before creating it — the suite runs on a long-lived DB
- Regression: with no fallbacks configured, every existing bouncer and filevault
  test passes unmodified

Rotation is simulated by patching the accessor in-process, **not** via
`th.server_settings`: that writes to the live `var/django.conf` and reloads the
server (`testit/helpers.py:826-853`), and stranding a `SECRET_KEY` override
there would break every later boot. This constraint is binding on the builder.

Run `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_helpers.test_secret_key_fallbacks`, then the
full default suite. Capture the baseline **before** the first edit per
`.claude/rules/build-baseline.md` and record it under `## Notes`.

### Documentation plan

- `docs/django_developer/helpers/crypto.md` — the rotation procedure: set the
  new `SECRET_KEY`, move the old one into `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, deploy, remove
  the fallback once old tokens have expired. State plainly what is covered
  (bouncer tokens, filevault, Django sessions/CSRF/password-reset) and what is
  not (`hash.py` stored hashes — needs a re-hash migration).
- `docs/django_developer/helpers/settings_reference.md` — add
  `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` beside `SECRET_KEY`, both with prose instead of bare
  bullets.
- `docs/django_developer/helpers/settings.md` — reinforce the `get` vs
  `get_static` rule at line 150 using `SECRET_KEY` as the worked example.
- `docs/django_developer/filevault/README.md` — the key-wrapping row: file-based
  key only, unwrap honors fallbacks.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — new capability plus the filevault fix, with a note to check
  for a `Setting` row named `SECRET_KEY` before upgrading.
- No `docs/web_developer/` change — nothing here is REST-visible.

### Size

4 source files (1 new), 1 new test file + 2 suites extended, 5 doc files. One
commit. No migrations, no model changes.

### Challenge

Red-teamed by an independent fresh-context agent against the **original**
hard-fail plan. Ian then cut that scope, which mooted several objections
outright. Dispositions carried into this version:

- **"No non-destructive recovery path; the error message's advice destroys
  data"** — *superseded, and it is why this item now exists.* The challenger
  showed consumer repos persist `SECRET_KEY`-derived material (filevault ekeys,
  camaccess master keys at `mojoware/server/apps/camware/camaccess/models/device.py:94`,
  mverify `ssn_hash`), so forcing a key change would brick it. The hard fail is
  gone; this item's entire purpose is now to *provide* the non-destructive path.
  Verified independently: `unwrap_ekey` has no dual-key fallback
  (`mojo/helpers/crypto/vault.py:157-172`).
- **"`SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` is unchecked"** — *amended into the objective.* The
  challenger flagged that an operator would naturally move the old key into
  `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` and that nothing in mojo honors it. Correct, and
  confirmed: no reference to it anywhere in this repo. That is now the item.
- **"filevault `get`→`get_static` is a one-way door"** — *amended.* Kept, with
  the challenger's requested guard: the CHANGELOG must tell operators to check
  for an existing `Setting` row named `SECRET_KEY` before upgrading, since files
  wrapped while such a row was live would become unwrappable. Challenger rated
  the odds low (nothing in django-mojo or the consumer repos creates one) but
  the cost of the warning is one line.
- **"The wiring test can't be written as described — `DjangoConfigLoader()`
  resolves `paths.VAR_ROOT` process-wide and tests run concurrently"**
  (`testit/runner.py:1434,1502`) — *moot*: no `load_settings_config` change
  remains. The underlying warning is preserved as the binding constraint in the
  Testing plan.
- **"The length warning is operationally a no-op — `logit.warning` writes to a
  file nobody reads"** (`mojo/helpers/logit.py:75-80`) — *moot*: no length check
  remains.
- **"Stale line references in the workspec"** — *amended*: `_validate_config_file`
  is `parser.py:29-32` (not 74-77) and `load_settings_profile` is `helper.py:27`
  (not 29). Corrected wherever they still appear.
- **"`load_settings_config` universality holds, but `wmx_api/config/settings/__init__.py:26-42`
  already assigns into `globals()` after the call"** — *recorded, no action.* No
  longer load-bearing, but a useful correction to the "always the last line"
  assumption if startup validation is ever revisited.
- **Sound, no objection**: `ImproperlyConfigured` as the type; `django-insecure-`,
  50 and 5 matching Django's constants; the lazy `logit` import being safe this
  early; `server_settings` never rewriting the `SECRET_KEY` line
  (`testit/helpers.py:608-635`) — independently re-verified.

One challenger claim was **rebutted**: that dropping the hard length floor was
justified but for the wrong reason. The challenger argued 16 random chars is
~95 bits and fine for HMAC-SHA256, so the "false-positive outage" framing was
self-undermining. That is correct on the crypto and it is now moot, but the
audit measured length only and could not distinguish a random 16-char key from a
typed one — so "insufficient evidence to hard-fail" remains the accurate reason
rather than "16 chars is fine".
